```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(logistf)
```

# Load and prepare data table for analyses 

```{r}
# 1. Load data, treating string variations of NA as true NAs
file_path <- "eeg_datatable_082126.xlsx"
raw_data <- read_excel(file_path, na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "n/a", "nan", "NaN"))

data_clean <- raw_data %>%
  # Filter out true NAs and any literal string matches
  filter(!is.na(Group) & !str_to_lower(str_trim(Group)) %in% c("", "n/a", "na", "nan")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Separate 4 groups into 2x2 factorial factors
    Injury = factor(if_else(str_detect(Group, "TBI"), "TBI", "Sham"), levels = c("Sham", "TBI")),
    SDs = factor(if_else(str_detect(Group, "\\+SD"), "SD", "Saline"), levels = c("Saline", "SD")),
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Sham", "Sham+SD", "TBI", "TBI+SD"))
  ) %>%
  # Drop any leftover unused factor levels
  droplevels()
```

# Function for binary count  (Pre and Post ptz periods)
Here we use the Firth's Penalized Logistic Regression
- this is like a standard Logistic regression, but it can handle 0% cases by introducing a penalty term to the Liklihood function

```{r}
# Binary analysis function: Subsets DV, drops NAs, runs Firth's 2-Way Logistic Regression + FDR Post-Hoc
run_binary_analysis_LOGISTIC <- function(data, dv_index) {
  dv_cols_local <- names(data)
  dv_name <- dv_cols_local[dv_index]
  
  cat("=======================================================\n")
  cat(sprintf("ANALYSIS FOR: %s (DV Index: %d, Column: %s)\n", 
              dv_name, dv_index, names(data)[dv_index]))
  cat("=======================================================\n\n")
  
  # Step A: Ensure DV is numeric
  data_subset <- data
  data_subset[[dv_name]] <- as.numeric(as.character(data_subset[[dv_name]]))
  
  # Step B: Report and drop excluded animals
  dropped_animals <- data_subset %>%
    filter(is.na(.data[[dv_name]])) %>%
    pull(Animal)
  
  if (length(dropped_animals) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("Dropped %d animal(s) due to NA in %s: %s\n\n", 
                length(dropped_animals), dv_name, paste(dropped_animals, collapse = ", ")))
  } else {
    cat("No animals dropped due to missing values.\n\n")
  }
  
  # Actually create subset with dropped animals
  analysis_df <- data_subset %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[dv_name]]))
  cat(sprintf("Final sample size for analysis: %d animals\n\n", nrow(analysis_df)))
  
  if (nrow(analysis_df) < 4) {
    cat("Insufficient data points to perform binary analysis.\n\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  # Step C: Summary of percent positive (seizure or spikes) per group
  summary_stats <- analysis_df %>%
    group_by(Group) %>%
    summarise(
      Total_Animals = n(),
      Count_Positive = sum(.data[[dv_name]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      Count_Negative = Total_Animals - Count_Positive,
      Pct_Positive = (Count_Positive / Total_Animals) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  cat("--- PERCENTAGE SUMMARY TABLE ---\n")
  print(as.data.frame(summary_stats))
  cat("\n")
  
  # Step D: 2-Way Factorial Firth's Penalized Logistic Regression (Injury * SDs)
  cat("--- 2-WAY FACTORIAL FIRTH LOGISTIC REGRESSION (Injury * SDs) ---\n")
  formula_str <- as.formula(sprintf("`%s` ~ Injury * SDs", dv_name))
  firth_model <- logistf(formula_str, data = analysis_df)
  print(summary(firth_model))
  cat("\n")
  
  # Step E: Pairwise Group Comparisons with Firth Penalization + FDR correction
  cat("--- PAIRWISE GROUP COMPARISONS (Firth Odds Ratio & FDR Adjusted p-values) ---\n")
  groups <- levels(analysis_df$Group)
  combos <- combn(groups, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  
  pairwise_res <- lapply(combos, function(pair) {
    sub_data <- analysis_df %>% 
      filter(Group %in% pair) %>% 
      mutate(Group = droplevels(Group))
    
    sub_formula <- as.formula(sprintf("`%s` ~ Group", dv_name))
    
    test <- tryCatch(
      logistf(sub_formula, data = sub_data),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    
    if (!is.null(test)) {
      # Coefficient index 2 corresponds to the second group level vs baseline
      beta <- coef(test)[2]
      odds_ratio <- exp(beta)
      p_val <- test$prob[2]
    } else {
      odds_ratio <- NA
      p_val <- NA
    }
    
    data.frame(
      Comparison = paste(pair[1], "vs", pair[2]),
      Odds_Ratio = round(odds_ratio, 3),
      p_value = round(p_val, 5),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }) %>% bind_rows()
  
  pairwise_res$p_adj_fdr <- round(p.adjust(pairwise_res$p_value, method = "fdr"), 5)
  print(pairwise_res)
  cat("\n")
  
  return(invisible(list(
    model = firth_model,
    post_hoc = pairwise_res, 
    summary = summary_stats, 
    data = analysis_df,
    dv_name = dv_name
  )))
}
```

```{r}
# Separate Plotting Function
plot_binary_contingency <- function(res, 
                                    title = NULL, 
                                    subtitle = NULL, 
                                    xlab = "Group", 
                                    ylab = "Proportion of Animals (%)",
                                    fill_colors = c("No Event (0)" = "#7f7f7f", "Event (1)" = "#d95f02"),
                                    legend_title = "Outcome") {
  
  if (is.null(res) || is.null(res$data)) {
    warning("No valid analysis data to plot.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  
  df <- res$data
  dv_name <- res$dv_name
  
  # Default titles if not supplied
  if (is.null(title)) {
    title <- paste("Contingency Proportion:", dv_name)
  }
  if (is.null(subtitle)) {
    subtitle <- paste("Omnibus Fisher p =", round(res$omnibus$p.value, 4))
  }
  
  plot_data <- df %>%
    mutate(Outcome = factor(if_else(.data[[dv_name]] == 1, "Event (1)", "No Event (0)"),
                            levels = c("No Event (0)", "Event (1)"))) %>%
    group_by(Group, Outcome) %>%
    summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
    mutate(
      Total = sum(Count),
      Proportion = Count / Total,
      Label = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", Count, Proportion * 100)
    )
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Group, y = Proportion, fill = Outcome)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.65, color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Label),
              position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.8, fontface = "bold", color = "white") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colors) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = xlab,
      y = ylab,
      fill = legend_title
    ) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "top",
      axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  
  print(p)
  return(invisible(p))
}
```


```{r}
res_1 <- run_binary_analysis_LOGISTIC(data_clean, dv_index = 4)

plot_binary_contingency(
  res = res_1,
  title = "Pre-PTZ Seizure Incidence",
  subtitle = "Firth Factorial Logistic Regression",
  xlab = "Experimental Group",
  ylab = "% of Animals",
  fill_colors = c("No Event (0)" = "#4A5568", "Event (1)" = "#A20000"),
  legend_title = "Seizure Status"
)
```

)
